lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to encrypt and decrypt messages with a Caesar cipher using letter positions and modular arithmetic.
Shift every letter a fixed number of places along the alphabet: with a shift of 3, a → d, b → e, h → k.
Find each letter’s position in the alphabet (a = 1 … z = 26) by searching the alphabet string — it’s linear search again!
The mod operator wraps numbers around, like a clock: ((position − 1 + shift) mod 26) + 1.
To decrypt, shift the other way (−3).
Caesar ciphers are easy to break — modern encryption uses maths that’s far harder to crack.
Python’s index finds the position; percent is mod. Same algorithm, fewer blocks.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
